statements.subject: client
statements.description: Once an SMTP client lexically identifies a domain to which mail will be delivered for processing (as described in Sections 2.3.5 and 3.6), a DNS lookup MUST be performed to resolve the domain name (RFC 1035 [2]).
actions: perform DNS lookup to resolve domain name

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Due to a history of problems, SMTP servers used for initial submission of messages SHOULD NOT make such inferences (Message Submission Servers [18] have somewhat more flexibility) and intermediate (relay) SMTP servers MUST NOT make them.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: Due to a history of problems, SMTP servers used for initial submission of messages SHOULD NOT make such inferences (Message Submission Servers [18] have somewhat more flexibility) and intermediate (relay) SMTP servers MUST NOT make them.

statements.subject: smtp
statements.description: If a non-existent domain error is returned, this situation MUST be reported as an error.
actions: report non-existent domain as error

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If a temporary error is returned, the message MUST be queued and retried later (see Section 4.5.4.1).
actions: queue message
schedule retry per Section 4.5.4.1

statements.subject: smtp
statements.description: If MX records are present, but none of them are usable, or the implicit MX is unusable, this situation MUST be reported as an error.
actions: report unusable MX records or unusable implicit MX as error

statements.subject: smtp
statements.description: If one or more MX RRs are found for a given name, SMTP systems MUST NOT utilize any address RRs associated with that name unless they are located using the MX RRs; the "implicit MX" rule above applies only if there are no MX records present.
actions: use only address RRs located via MX RRs

statements.subject: smtp
statements.description: If MX records are present, but none of them are usable, this situation MUST be reported as an error.
actions: report unusable MX records as error

statements.subject: smtp
statements.description: When a domain name associated with an MX RR is looked up and the associated data field obtained, the data field of that response MUST contain a domain name.

statements.subject: smtp
statements.description: That domain name, when queried, MUST return at least one address record (e.g., A or AAAA RR) that gives the IP address of the SMTP server to which the message should be directed.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: To provide reliable mail transmission, the SMTP client MUST be able to try (and retry) each of the relevant addresses in this list in order, until a delivery attempt succeeds.
actions: try each address in list in order
retry next address on delivery failure
stop when delivery attempt succeeds

statements.subject: smtp
statements.description: However, there MAY also be a configurable limit on the number of alternate addresses that can be tried.

statements.subject: client
statements.description: In any case, the SMTP client SHOULD try at least two addresses.
actions: try at least two addresses from the list

statements.subject: smtp
statements.description: MX records contain a preference indication that MUST be used in sorting if more than one such record appears (see below).
actions: sort MX records by preference value

statements.subject: client
statements.description: If there are multiple destinations with the same preference and there is no clear reason to favor one (e.g., by recognition of an easily reached address), then the sender-SMTP MUST randomize them to spread the load across multiple mail exchangers for a specific organization.
actions: randomize MX destinations with equal preference value

statements.subject: client
statements.description: It is the responsibility of the domain name resolver interface to have ordered this list by decreasing preference if necessary, and the SMTP sender MUST try them in the order presented.
actions: try multihomed host addresses in the order presented by the resolver

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If an SMTP server receives a message with a destination for which it is a designated Mail eXchanger, it MAY relay the message (potentially after having rewritten the MAIL FROM and/or RCPT TO addresses), make final delivery of the message, or hand it off using some mechanism outside the SMTP-provided transport environment.
actions: relay message
or make final delivery of message
or hand off via external mechanism

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If it determines that it should relay the message without rewriting the address, it MUST sort the MX records to determine candidates for delivery.
actions: sort MX records by preference to determine delivery candidates

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The relay host MUST then inspect the list for any of the names or addresses by which it might be known in mail transactions.
actions: inspect sorted MX list for own names or addresses

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If a matching record is found, all records at that preference level and higher-numbered ones MUST be discarded from consideration.
actions: discard all MX records at matching preference level
discard all MX records at higher-numbered preference levels

statements.subject: message
statements.description: If there are no records left at that point, it is an error condition, and the message MUST be returned as undeliverable.
actions: return message as undeliverable

statements.subject: server
statements.description: If records do remain, they SHOULD be tried, best preference first, as described above.
actions: try remaining MX records in best-preference-first order
